claims.text: A controlled dwell during rapid heating improves inter-element mixing in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Improved inter-element mixing and uniform nucleation stabilize a single-phase solid solution.
Under uninterrupted rapid heating and cooling, these nanoparticles typically exhibit phase separation and elemental segregation.
Under uninterrupted rapid heating and cooling, these nanoparticles typically exhibit irregular morphology and broad particle-size distributions.
The proposed intervention is a brief controlled dwell at an intermediate temperature during rapid heating.
The dwell temperature should be below the onset of thermal decomposition but high enough to activate atomic diffusion.
The proposed compositional regime is near-equiatomic and contains more than five noble metals.
A brief dwell provides enough atomic mobility to overcome kinetic diffusion barriers that otherwise trap compositional inhomogeneities during rapid processing.
Dwell-enabled diffusion promotes inter-element mixing and uniform nucleation.
Dwell-enabled mixing and uniform nucleation counteract phase separation and morphological irregularity.
Relative to uninterrupted rapid heating and cooling, the dwell will improve phase uniformity.
Relative to uninterrupted rapid heating and cooling, the dwell will reduce elemental segregation.
Relative to uninterrupted rapid heating and cooling, the dwell will narrow the particle-size distribution.
Below the effective diffusion-activation window, the dwell may provide insufficient mixing.
Excessive diffusion outside the proposed processing window may produce unwanted phases.
